question: What filesystem access-control contract should OpenClaw support for host file tools and exec: a full allow/deny path policy, a file-tool-only policy with explicit exec exclusion, or Docker/OS-user isolation only?
rationale: The code gap is clear, but choosing the permanent config surface and security boundary changes operator expectations and cannot be safely automated.

options.title: Define a versioned path policy
options.body: Specify a `tools.fs` or successor policy with allowed paths, denied paths, normalization, symlink handling, default behavior, docs, tests, and an explicit exec strategy before landing an implementation.

options.title: Ship file-tool-only first
options.body: Accept a narrower PathGuard-style policy for read/write/edit/media while documenting exec as separate and keeping https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/74379 open.

options.title: Reject config ACLs
options.body: Close this direction and state that strong filesystem isolation must use Docker, VMs, or separate OS users rather than OpenClaw path ACLs.

recommendation.title: Define a versioned path policy
recommendation.body: Specify a `tools.fs` or successor policy with allowed paths, denied paths, normalization, symlink handling, default behavior, docs, tests, and an explicit exec strategy before landing an implementation.
